_note: Search coverage for the public talks archive. A later pass should expand sampled areas, then mark an area exhausted only when new finds dry up. A first YouTube results page is sampled, not exhausted, unless that query returned nothing relevant.
event_linking: After talks are written here, python3 tools/event_backfill.py looks up an existing calendar or backfill event on series, date span, city, country and organiser, then creates a previous event when the video page states the day, the place, the type and the organiser. A talk that cannot be dated or placed stays unlinked with unlink_reason.

runs.notes: 1131 unique videos from the first page of 72 YouTube searches were screened by title and channel. 160 of those had the watch page opened in the capped pass, and 22 further ids were opened in a targeted pass. One video (Andreas M. Antonopoulos at Oslo Blockchain Day 2017) was opened from its URL directly, so candidates_checked is 1132 and watch_pages_opened is 183. 74 talks were kept. YouTube's watch-page player asked for a sign-in and omitted lengthSeconds; duration is the lengthText on YouTube's own search result for that video id, except yt-eo-0BgrKxiI, which was not in a search result and has a null duration. embed is the YouTube oEmbed iframe flag. Spoken language was not labelled on the pages we kept, so language is null. Talks are linked by tools/event_backfill.py after they are stored: an existing event is tried first, and a previous event is created only from facts the video page stated. The October 2026 Oslo Nexa meetup has no recording yet. Baltic Honeybadger (Riga) was skipped. Predatory conference mills were filtered. FO, GL and AX were searched; the first-page hits were not public crypto talks held there, so those countries stay sampled with zero talks, not exhausted.
